messages:
maria: Hey — hitting a weird combo of issues in the python async sample app for Dedicated/VPC onboarding. When a corporate HTTP_PROXY is set plus a custom CA, the async client ignores REDWOOD_BASE_URL and also fails SSL verification. Repro steps below.

maria: env: 
  REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://dedicated-nyc.corp.internal
  REDWOOD_CUSTOM_CA=/tmp/company-root.pem
  HTTP_PROXY=http://corp-proxy:3128
  USE_ASYNC=1

maria: Code (very small):
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()  # expects env-driven base_url + custom CA
await client.chat.create("hello")
```

maria: Error (stack):
```
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:XXXX)
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
httpx.ConnectError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='api.redwood.ai', port=443): Max retries exceeded...
```

maria: Note: the sync client (redwood.Client) works fine with the same env vars. Async goes to api.redwood.ai (public) even though REDWOOD_BASE_URL is set.

cheng: can you paste the exact env var name you set? we support REDWOOD_BASE_URL and REDWOOD_CUSTOM_CA, right?

maria: yep exact ones above. Sync client respects them. It's only reproable when HTTP_PROXY is present.

sam: quick hypothesis: our sync path uses requests.Session + ssl context built from REDWOOD_CUSTOM_CA / REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE; async path uses httpx.AsyncClient but we never wire the custom cafile into the AsyncTransport's ssl context when a proxy is active. also proxy env handling can change request URL vs host headers.

sam: workaround you can try locally:
```py
import ssl, httpx
ssl_ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/tmp/company-root.pem')
async with httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(ssl_context=ssl_ctx, proxies={"https": "http://corp-proxy:3128"})) as ac:
    r = await ac.get('https://dedicated-nyc.corp.internal/health')
    print(r.status_code)
```

maria: tried the workaround, that fixes SSL verification but the SDK still routed to api.redwood.ai until I explicitly passed base_url into AsyncClient(..., base_url=...). So two issues: 1) custom CA not propagated into httpx transport automatically, 2) base_url/env precedence gets lost when proxying.

kb: Good catch. I dug into the SDK async client init — we call httpx.AsyncClient(proxies=..., transport=...) in different code paths and sometimes construct the request URL using proxy-aware logic that reconstructs absolute URL from the proxy host; that code defaults to the public host when base_url is None and then reads it off the request object in a way that has a race with environment-based proxy rewriting. TL;DR: explicit base_url param should always win, and env var should be canonical fallback.

sam: I'll open a small fix. Plan: (A) ensure we always set httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=explicit_or_env) early; (B) build ssl.SSLContext from REDWOOD_CUSTOM_CA and pass into AsyncHTTPTransport when any proxy is configured; (C) add a typed overload in our client stubs so mypy knows transport/ssl kwargs are allowed for AsyncClient. Will put up PR #4302.

maria: thanks — landed a quick local patch from Sam's snippet and confirmed both base_url and CA are respected now. sample-app CI still fails on macOS runner (cert store differences) but linux passes.

cheng: please add a small integration test that spins up a tiny proxy (httpbin proxy) and an internal TLS server with our CA to catch regressions in the future. Also update the onboard README for sample-app to mention the explicit env var preference and the fallback behavior.

kb: typing note: mypy complains because our AsyncClient.__init__ signature in py.typed doesn't include transport kw; adding Protocol/overloads for sync vs async ctor params should fix it. leave a TODO in the PR.

sam: PR #4302 opened and assigned to eng/devex, includes tests + docs + typing tweaks. cc @maria for QA.

maria: thanks — will smoke-test on mac runner tomorrow. leaving a follow-up issue for packaging of the sample-app docker image with our CA baked in. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy check — sample-app-ci: linux-integration ✅, macos-integration ❌ (certificate path issue)

maria: noted. i'll pick up the macos follow-up after this fix is merged.

cheng: great, thanks all.
